answer.rationale: Hard constraint is no added delivery risk: contract ends in 14 days with no auto-renew and the line sits at 94% with zero buffer, so switch, defer, or a new second source would put continuity at risk. Incumbent continuity historically avoided migration and delivery breaks (c1). Cost pressure is addressed by renegotiating at this renewal—prior renewal benchmarking moved price and terms (c4) and multi-year volume terms cut unit cost without shrinking scope (c6)—without changing the primary source. Whether that path can deliver a full 18% cut is unknown; failed talks before expiry are a real supply-gap risk, so this is a structured negotiation on the existing primary, not a vendor change or a deferral. Verifying c4 as the load-bearing analog.
